source.stem: Decide whether the following statements are correct. Mark “√” for correct answers and “×” for wrong answers. (1) Objects that can move must be living things.

hinge.title: Compare nutrition labels to decide which packaged food better fits the junk-food pattern, using calories, fats, proteins, and dietary fibre.

intelligence.enrichment: Foods with high calories due to high sugar and fat and very low amounts of proteins, minerals, vitamins, and dietary fibres are called junk foods; potato wafers have 536 kcal, 35.0 g fat, 7.0 g protein, and 4.8 g dietary fibre per 100 g, while roasted chana has 355 kcal, 6.26 g fat, 18.64 g protein, and 16.8 g dietary fibre per 100 g. higher energy and fat with lower protein and dietary fibre on the label -> stronger match to the junk-food pattern The learner correctly applies this rule: Foods with high calories due to high sugar and fat and very low amounts of proteins, minerals, vitamins, and dietary fibres are called junk foods; potato wafers have 536 kcal, 35.0 g fat, 7.0 g protein, and 4.8 g dietary fibre per 100 g, while roasted chana has 355 kcal, 6.26 g fat, 18.64 g protein, and 16.8 g dietary fibre per 100 g. The food with the biggest single number on the label is automatically the junk food.
